title: Existentially closed extensions and model companions
summary: Build models containing every existential witness available in a further model extension, and characterize when these models form a model companion.
abstract: A strict linear order can be enlarged by inserting a point into a gap or adding a point past an endpoint. The dense orders without endpoints have already met all these demands. More generally, a model is existentially closed when any finite pattern that can be realized in a further model extension already has witnesses inside it. For theories preserved under increasing unions, we construct such an extension of every model by repeatedly handling possible requests, including requests involving newly added elements. We then prove that a model companion exists exactly when these existentially closed models can themselves be described by first-order axioms. Dense linear orders provide the concrete example, while a single pass over an original model shows why the construction must revisit new parameters.
